examples.question_text: A circle has radius $4\text{ cm}$. A chord subtends a minor central angle of $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ radians. Find the exact perimeter of the minor segment.
examples.solution_text:
The perimeter is the minor arc plus the chord.
$\begin{align*}l&=r\theta\\&=4\times\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=\frac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
By cosine rule:
$\begin{align*}c^{2}&=4^{2}+4^{2}-2(4)(4)\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=48\\c&=4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P&=l+c\\&=\left(\frac{8\pi}{3}+4\sqrt{3}\right)\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A windscreen wiper sweeps between concentric arcs of radii $24\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ through $150^{\circ}$. Find the exact area swept.
examples.solution_text:
$\theta=150\times\dfrac{\pi}{180}=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ radians.
Subtract the inner sector from the outer sector.
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(24^{2})\frac{5\pi}{6}-\frac12(12^{2})\frac{5\pi}{6}\\&=\frac12(576-144)\frac{5\pi}{6}\\&=180\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A sector has area $10\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$ and arc length $5\pi\text{ cm}$. Find its exact radius $r$ and central angle $\theta$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}r\theta&=5\pi\\\frac12r^{2}\theta&=10\pi\end{align*}$
Substitute $r\theta=5\pi$ into the area equation.
$\begin{align*}\frac12r(5\pi)&=10\pi\\r&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}4\theta&=5\pi\\\theta&=\frac{5\pi}{4}\text{ radians}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A sector subtending $135^{\circ}$ is removed from a circle of radius $8\text{ cm}$. Find the exact area remaining.

examples.solution_text:
$r=5+5=10\text{ cm}$.
A perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord and its central angle. Let $\alpha=\angle AON$.
$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=\frac{5}{10}=\frac12\\\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\\theta&=2\alpha=\frac{2\pi}{3}\end{align*}$
Subtract the triangle area from the sector area.
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{segment}}&=\frac12(10^{2})\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac12(10^{2})\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=\left(\frac{100\pi}{3}-25\sqrt3\right)\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A sector has area $20\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$ and central angle $\dfrac{5\pi}{8}$ radians. Find its exact radius.

examples.solution_text:
Find the sector radius using cosine rule in triangle $ABD$.
$\begin{align*}BD^{2}&=4^{2}+4^{2}-2(4)(4)\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=48\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_{\triangle}&=\frac12(4)(4)\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\\&=4\sqrt3\text{ m}^{2}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac12(BD^{2})\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=8\pi\text{ m}^{2}\end{align*}$
$A_{\text{garden}}=(4\sqrt3+8\pi)\text{ m}^{2}$.

Each arc has radius $3\text{ cm}$ and central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
$\begin{align*}l&=3\frac{\pi}{3}=\pi\text{ cm}\\P&=3\pi\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
The enclosed region is the triangle plus three equal segments.
$\begin{align*}A_{\triangle}&=\frac12(3^{2})\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{segment}}&=\frac12(3^{2})\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}\\&=\frac{3\pi}{2}-\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}+3\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}-\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}\right)\\&=\frac92(\pi-\sqrt3)\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A chord of length $7\text{ cm}$ lies in a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$. Find the minor central angle to three decimal places and the minor arc length to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Use cosine rule in the triangle formed by the chord and two radii.
$\begin{align*}7^{2}&=5^{2}+5^{2}-2(5)(5)\cos\theta\\\cos\theta&=\frac{1}{50}\\\theta&=\arccos\frac{1}{50}\\&\approx1.551\text{ radians}\end{align*}$
Use the unrounded angle for the arc length.
$\begin{align*}l&=r\theta\\&=5\arccos\frac{1}{50}\\&\approx7.75\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Minor arc length is 4(2π/3)=8π/3 cm. Cosine rule gives c²=16+16−32cos(2π/3)=48, so c=4√3 cm. Perimeter is (8π/3+4√3) cm.
150°=5π/6 radians. Outer sector minus inner sector gives A=(1/2)(576−144)(5π/6)=180π cm².
Using rθ=5π in (1/2)r²θ=10π gives (5π/2)r=10π, hence r=4 cm. Then θ=5π/4 radians, a valid sector angle.
The remaining angle is 225°=5π/4 radians. Its area is (1/2)(64)(5π/4)=40π cm².

OM = ON + NM = 10 cm. In right triangle ONA, cos(alpha) = ON/OA = 5/10 = 1/2, so alpha = pi/3 and the minor central angle is 2pi/3. Sector area = (1/2)(100)(2pi/3) = 100pi/3 cm². Triangle area = (1/2)(100)sin(2pi/3) = 25sqrt(3) cm². Minor segment area = (100pi/3 − 25sqrt(3)) cm². The diagram coordinates agree with both radial distances, the perpendicular chord and the angle calculation; the relocated N label avoids the dimension labels and right-angle marker.
20π=(1/2)r²(5π/8) gives r²=64. The positive radius is 8 cm.

Cosine rule gives BD²=16+16−32cos(2π/3)=48. Triangle area is 8sin(2π/3)=4√3 m²; sector area is (1/2)(48)(π/3)=8π m². Total area is (4√3+8π) m². Diagram coordinates give AB=AD=4, angle DAB=2π/3, equal sector radii and angle DBC=π/3, with the regions on opposite sides of BD.

Each radius-3 arc subtends π/3, giving perimeter 3π cm. Triangle area is 9√3/4 cm². Each added segment has area 3π/2−9√3/4 cm². Total area is (9/2)(π−√3) cm². The three authored arcs have the stated opposite-vertex centres and form the required boundary.
49=50−50cos θ gives cos θ=1/50. Thus θ=arccos(0.02)=1.550794993… radians, rounding to 1.551. The unrounded angle gives l=5θ=7.753974967… cm, rounding to 7.75 cm.
